text.TITLE: The Fighting Temeraire (after Turner)
text.TASK_MD: paint the picture shown in `/app/target.png` (a square crop of J. M. W. Turner's The Fighting Temeraire, 1839) onto the main sheet with brush and oil paints, **in at most 2360 strokes**.
text.ENGINE_U:
at every physics step (100 Hz) the tip over a sheet is one motion event for libmypaint 1.6.1 with the
  mypaint-brushes preset `tanda/oil-03-paint` made pointed (dab size scaled to the paper; the preset's random dab offset and
  tracking noise follow the pressure like the dab size, so a light press draws a thin line; the frozen preset is the instance's
  `brush.preset_json`): a wet oil paint whose mark depends on the **pressure** (press depth / 15 mm: straight strokes are about
  2 mm wide at a 1.25 mm press, 2.5 mm at 1.5 mm, 3 mm at 2 mm, 4.2 mm at 3 mm, 6 mm at 4 mm, 8 mm at 5 mm and 11 mm from 6 mm on;
  a lighter press thins and fades the line), the **speed**, the **direction** (the elliptical dabs follow it) and the engine's own
  smudging and jitter (deterministic): strokes pick up and blend the wet paint already on the sheet, and later strokes lie over
  earlier ones. The engine is `MyPaintPainter` in `/opt/tools/rcb_brush.py` (+ `/opt/mypaint`). One continuous contact is one
  **stroke**; paint is permanent (only `s.reset()` clears it).
text.ENGINE_L:
- Wherever the loaded tip is below a sheet's surface the brush paints wet oil paint; what the mark looks like depends on how you
  press, move and turn the brush, and it blends with wet paint already on the sheet (the practice sheet is there to find out). One
  continuous contact of the loaded brush with the main sheet is one **stroke**. The arm is position-controlled (PD, 20 Hz targets):
  a moving target is followed with a lag.
text.SCORE_U: - The grader compares the main sheet with the picture: the painting is compared with the picture after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis (translation only; if the best shift reaches that limit, the sheet is scored unshifted); the metrics are then taken only inside the sheet's central area, 8 mm in from every edge (the border band is not scored); both blurred (σ = 1 mm); **ΔE** = the CIELAB colour difference (ΔE*ab) per pixel over the region where either has paint (dilated by 2 mm; the picture covers the whole sheet, so: the whole scored area): its mean and 90th percentile; **SSIM** of the lightness L* (σ 1.5 mm windows); **edge correlation** = the correlation of the lightness-gradient magnitudes of the two blurred pictures; **paint IoU** = the painted fraction of the scored area (paint coverage ≥ 0.5); the **number of strokes** on the main sheet (painted contacts). **Success iff mean ΔE ≤ 99.0, p90 ΔE ≤ 99.0, SSIM ≥ 0.0, edge correlation ≥ -1.0, paint IoU ≥ 0.0 and at most 2360 strokes.** `final_reward` = max(0, 1 - mean ΔE / 20) (scaled by 2360 / strokes above 2360). Reported as well: the mean ΔE after a 4 mm blur, the SSIM at a 0.5 mm blur, and per colour region of the picture (the connected areas nearest to one paint, at least 30 mm²) the fraction within ΔE 10: the minimum and the area-weighted mean. The shift found is reported too (`register_dx_mm`, `register_dy_mm`: mm along the picture's columns and rows). `s.score()` returns exactly these metrics for the current sheet: a scoring service (a separate container) replays the actions you have executed since your last `s.reset()` and scores the resulting sheet.
text.SCORE_L: - The grader compares the main sheet with the picture: the painting is compared with the picture after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis (translation only; if the best shift reaches that limit, the sheet is scored unshifted); the metrics are then taken only inside the sheet's central area, 8 mm in from every edge (the border band is not scored); both blurred (σ = 1 mm); **ΔE** = the CIELAB colour difference (ΔE*ab) per pixel over the region where either has paint (dilated by 2 mm; the picture covers the whole sheet, so: the whole scored area): its mean and 90th percentile; **SSIM** of the lightness L* (σ 1.5 mm windows); **edge correlation** = the correlation of the lightness-gradient magnitudes of the two blurred pictures; **paint IoU** = the painted fraction of the scored area (paint coverage ≥ 0.5); the **number of strokes** on the main sheet (painted contacts). **Success iff mean ΔE ≤ 99.0, p90 ΔE ≤ 99.0, SSIM ≥ 0.0, edge correlation ≥ -1.0, paint IoU ≥ 0.0 and at most 2360 strokes** (the recorded episode is replayed twice and both replays must agree). The continuous score is max(0, 1 - mean ΔE / 20) (scaled by 2360 / strokes above 2360). Reported as well: the mean ΔE after a 4 mm blur, the SSIM at a 0.5 mm blur, and per colour region of the picture (the connected areas nearest to one paint, at least 30 mm²) the fraction within ΔE 10: the minimum and the area-weighted mean.
text.SRC: The picture is a public-domain painting, J. M. W. Turner, *The Fighting Temeraire* (1839; Wikimedia Commons `File:The Fighting Temeraire, JMW Turner, National Gallery.jpg`, Public domain), cropped to a square and downscaled to the sheet
text.DESC_TOML_U: RoboPaint oil painting from a reference: embodied robotic painting (ManiSkill 3.0.1 Franka Panda with an oil-paint brush; the paint is libmypaint 1.6.1 with the mypaint-brushes preset tanda/oil-03-paint made pointed, wet paint that smudges and blends): produce one replayable trajectory that paints the picture target.png (a square crop of J. M. W. Turner's The Fighting Temeraire, 1839) onto the main sheet with 16 premixed paints, in at most 2360 strokes. Scored at a 1 mm scale against the picture (success iff mean CIELAB ΔE <= 99.0, p90 ΔE <= 99.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.0, edge correlation >= -1.0, paint IoU >= 0.0 (all after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, inside the central area 8 mm in from the sheet's edges) and at most 2360 strokes; 1 - mean ΔE / 20 is the continuous score); the thresholds are the reference solution's robot execution with a margin. s.score() is served by a separate scoring container.
text.DESC_TOML_L: RoboPaint oil painting from a reference, STANDARD MODE (robot as a service, eai-standard/2.2): embodied robotic oil painting (ManiSkill 3.0.1 Franka Panda with an oil-paint brush; libmypaint 1.6.1 paints) on the same frozen instance as the privileged task: paint the picture target.png (a square crop of J. M. W. Turner's The Fighting Temeraire, 1839) onto the main sheet in at most 2360 strokes, with 16 premixed paints and a practice sheet for test strokes. The agent only gets a client: get_obs (camera RGB + proprioception), submit (ee_pose or joint_position chunks). No reset, no sheet readout, no brush model, no score; the sim service records the episode, which is replayed twice and scored at a 1 mm scale against the picture (success iff mean CIELAB ΔE <= 99.0, p90 ΔE <= 99.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.0, edge correlation >= -1.0, paint IoU >= 0.0 (all after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, inside the central area 8 mm in from the sheet's edges) and at most 2360 strokes).

text.README_INSTANCE: paint the picture in `environment/target.png` (a square crop of J. M. W. Turner's The Fighting Temeraire, 1839: a public-domain masterpiece, cropped and downscaled to the 227 mm main sheet) in at most 2360 strokes, with 16 premixed paints (the picture's colours quantised) on a plate and a practice sheet beside it; the brush starts dry; start pose = PandaStick's rest keyframe; everything frozen in `environment/instance.json`
text.GOAL_MD: Paint the picture: mean CIELAB ΔE <= 99.0, p90 ΔE <= 99.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.0, edge correlation >= -1.0, paint IoU >= 0.0 (all after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, inside the central area 8 mm in from the sheet's edges) and at most 2360 strokes. `final_reward` = max(0, 1 - mean ΔE / 20) (× 2360 / strokes above 2360).
text.DIFF_MD: There is no exact solution: the picture is a real painting, the paint is wet (strokes pick up and blend what is under them), the brush makes 2-11 mm marks (the fine ones need a light, exact press), 16 premixed paints are all there is, and fine work costs robot time: the reference solution's 1580 strokes take 45 of the episode's 60 simulated minutes (53438 of the 72000 control steps). The rule is set by the reference solution executed by this robot, with a margin; the measured axes are in task.toml [metadata].
text.REF_MD: The reference solution is our baseline painter's stroke program (`solution/program.json`, made at generation time by a stroke optimiser with libmypaint in the loop against the picture: a ground of parallel rows in the nearest paints, then 4 layers of curved strokes along the picture's isophotes with ever lighter presses (marks of about 6, 3.6, 2.6 and 2.1 mm), placed where the canvas is furthest from the picture, each paint's strokes of a layer in a nearest-neighbour order) executed by the robot (`solution/ref_oil.py` with the program's `motion`: a 6 mm hover between strokes, quick dips, short holds); the rule was calibrated on exactly that execution (`solution/calibration.json`). The plan is frozen at generation time (`solution/oracle_qpos.npy`); `solution/solve.sh` replays it:
text.L_ORACLE: `solution/`: streams the privileged reference solution's joint targets (one row per control step, `hold`) as `joint_position` chunks; the recorded trajectory then equals the privileged one
text.RULE_SHORT: mean CIELAB ΔE <= 99.0, p90 ΔE <= 99.0, SSIM of L* >= 0.0, edge correlation >= -1.0, paint IoU >= 0.0 (all after the best single shift of the sheet, at most 5 mm along each axis, inside the central area 8 mm in from the sheet's edges) and at most 2360 strokes
text.CHANGELOG: - 2026-10-09: the hi-res version (docs/benchmarks/robopaint.md, Oil: the pointed brush). The brush is `tanda/oil-03-paint` made pointed: a light press draws a 2-3 mm line (before, every mark was 5-11 mm wide). The reference solution is a new program of 1573 strokes (was 299); executed by the robot it scores mean ΔE 3.49, SSIM 0.894 and edge correlation 0.646 against the picture (was 4.06, 0.860, 0.441). The rule is recalibrated on it with the same margins, except SSIM - 0.04 (was - 0.03): mean ΔE <= 3.9 (was 4.5), p90 ΔE <= 6.5 (was 8.0), SSIM >= 0.85 (was 0.83), edge correlation >= 0.59 (was 0.39); at most 2360 strokes (was 449); a path of at most 51400 mm (was 28100 mm). The picture, the scene's geometry and the scoring code are unchanged; results before this date are not comparable with this version.

optimiser.painter: the greedy layered painter of agent P (Hertzmann-style curved strokes along the isophotes, each layer planned against the canvas libmypaint really produced) on O's rows ground, each paint's strokes of a layer in a nearest-neighbour order
